title: nOS — Pulse (scheduled jobs, and the ones that stopped)
description: Every declared job and every run, from pulse_jobs and pulse_runs. Companion to tools/red-status.py, which answers what is red now rather than what has happened.

options.content:
**Pulse — the estate's scheduled-job organ, from `pulse_jobs` and `pulse_runs`.** 56 000 runs had accumulated with no Grafana surface at all; `tools/red-status.py` answers *what is red now*, and this answers *what has been happening*.

The question it exists for is the one CLAUDE.md tells the story of: **a nightly job that stops firing looks exactly like a nightly job with nothing to report.** A notification is an event and silence is a state, so the first row counts jobs that are declared, unpaused, and quiet — and a paused job is shown separately with its reason, because a deliberate pause is not a failure and must not be summed with one.

**A non-zero exit is not always a failure.** `pulse_jobs.findings_exit_codes` lists the codes a job uses to mean *I found something* — `discovery:contradiction-scan` exits 1 on a contradiction, which is the detector working. Every panel here reads that column; the first draft did not, and put a healthy detector at the top of the failure list. A run with `finished_at IS NULL` is counted as neither.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS jobs FROM pulse_jobs WHERE removed_at IS NULL AND paused = 0
targets.queryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS jobs FROM pulse_jobs WHERE removed_at IS NULL AND paused = 0

panels.title: Declared and silent
panels.description: Unpaused jobs that have NEVER produced a run. A schedule nothing fires is the estate's signature defect: it looks identical to a job with nothing to say. Zero is the only acceptable value.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_ran FROM pulse_jobs j WHERE j.removed_at IS NULL AND j.paused = 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pulse_runs r WHERE r.job_id = j.id)
targets.queryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_ran FROM pulse_jobs j WHERE j.removed_at IS NULL AND j.paused = 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pulse_runs r WHERE r.job_id = j.id)

panels.title: Overdue by a day
panels.description: Wing computes `next_fire_at`. A live job whose next fire is more than a day in the past has stopped being scheduled — the daemon is down, the cron is unparsable, or the job errored out of its own loop.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS overdue FROM pulse_jobs WHERE removed_at IS NULL AND paused = 0 AND next_fire_at IS NOT NULL AND julianday(next_fire_at) < julianday('now') - 1
targets.queryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS overdue FROM pulse_jobs WHERE removed_at IS NULL AND paused = 0 AND next_fire_at IS NOT NULL AND julianday(next_fire_at) < julianday('now') - 1

panels.title: Runs that never finished
panels.description: Fired over an hour ago, `finished_at` still NULL. The runner died between fire and finish, so nothing wrote an exit code — and a run with no exit code is not a failure anyone was told about.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_finished FROM pulse_runs WHERE finished_at IS NULL AND julianday(fired_at) < julianday('now') - 0.05
targets.queryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_finished FROM pulse_runs WHERE finished_at IS NULL AND julianday(fired_at) < julianday('now') - 0.05

panels.title: Runs per day, by outcome (30 d)
panels.description: Stacked. `unfinished` is its own band rather than folded into either side — it is the shape a crashing runner makes.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT substr(r.fired_at,1,10) AS day, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ok, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code IS NOT NULL AND r.exit_code <> 0 AND ',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(j.findings_exit_codes, '[]'), '[', ''), ']', ''), ' ', '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || r.exit_code || ',%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS found, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code IS NOT NULL AND r.exit_code <> 0 AND NOT ',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(j.findings_exit_codes, '[]'), '[', ''), ']', ''), ' ', '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || r.exit_code || ',%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed, SUM(CASE WHEN r.finished_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unfinished FROM pulse_runs r LEFT JOIN pulse_jobs j ON j.id = r.job_id WHERE julianday(r.fired_at) > julianday('now') - 30 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day
targets.queryText: SELECT substr(r.fired_at,1,10) AS day, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ok, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code IS NOT NULL AND r.exit_code <> 0 AND ',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(j.findings_exit_codes, '[]'), '[', ''), ']', ''), ' ', '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || r.exit_code || ',%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS found, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code IS NOT NULL AND r.exit_code <> 0 AND NOT ',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(j.findings_exit_codes, '[]'), '[', ''), ']', ''), ' ', '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || r.exit_code || ',%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed, SUM(CASE WHEN r.finished_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unfinished FROM pulse_runs r LEFT JOIN pulse_jobs j ON j.id = r.job_id WHERE julianday(r.fired_at) > julianday('now') - 30 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day

panels.title: Failure rate by job (30 d), worst first
panels.description: A NON-ZERO EXIT IS NOT ALWAYS A FAILURE, and `pulse_jobs` already said so: `findings_exit_codes` lists the codes a job uses to mean *I found something*. The first draft of this panel ignored that column and reported `discovery:contradiction-scan` as failing 16 of 24 runs — a working detector, top of the list, on the surface an operator uses to decide what to fix. `found` and `failed` are separate columns here and the sort is on `failed`.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT r.job_id AS job, COUNT(*) AS runs, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ok, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code IS NOT NULL AND r.exit_code <> 0 AND ',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(j.findings_exit_codes, '[]'), '[', ''), ']', ''), ' ', '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || r.exit_code || ',%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS found, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code IS NOT NULL AND r.exit_code <> 0 AND NOT ',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(j.findings_exit_codes, '[]'), '[', ''), ']', ''), ' ', '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || r.exit_code || ',%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed, MAX(r.fired_at) AS last_fired FROM pulse_runs r LEFT JOIN pulse_jobs j ON j.id = r.job_id WHERE julianday(r.fired_at) > julianday('now') - 30 GROUP BY r.job_id HAVING failed + found > 0 ORDER BY failed DESC, found DESC LIMIT 20
targets.queryText: SELECT r.job_id AS job, COUNT(*) AS runs, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ok, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code IS NOT NULL AND r.exit_code <> 0 AND ',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(j.findings_exit_codes, '[]'), '[', ''), ']', ''), ' ', '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || r.exit_code || ',%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS found, SUM(CASE WHEN r.exit_code IS NOT NULL AND r.exit_code <> 0 AND NOT ',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(j.findings_exit_codes, '[]'), '[', ''), ']', ''), ' ', '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || r.exit_code || ',%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed, MAX(r.fired_at) AS last_fired FROM pulse_runs r LEFT JOIN pulse_jobs j ON j.id = r.job_id WHERE julianday(r.fired_at) > julianday('now') - 30 GROUP BY r.job_id HAVING failed + found > 0 ORDER BY failed DESC, found DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Time since each job last fired
panels.description: The staleness column. A weekly job at 6 days is fine; the same job at 20 is a job that has quietly stopped, and no notification would have said so — the repeat-failure rule that stops a per-minute job flooding the inbox also stops a weekly one repeating news that still holds.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT j.id AS job, j.schedule, COALESCE(MAX(r.fired_at), 'never') AS last_fired, CAST(julianday('now') - julianday(MAX(r.fired_at)) AS INT) AS days_since FROM pulse_jobs j LEFT JOIN pulse_runs r ON r.job_id = j.id WHERE j.removed_at IS NULL AND j.paused = 0 GROUP BY j.id ORDER BY days_since DESC LIMIT 20
targets.queryText: SELECT j.id AS job, j.schedule, COALESCE(MAX(r.fired_at), 'never') AS last_fired, CAST(julianday('now') - julianday(MAX(r.fired_at)) AS INT) AS days_since FROM pulse_jobs j LEFT JOIN pulse_runs r ON r.job_id = j.id WHERE j.removed_at IS NULL AND j.paused = 0 GROUP BY j.id ORDER BY days_since DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Paused jobs, and why
panels.description: A pause is an operator decision and belongs beside the failures, not in them. A row here with no reason is a job somebody switched off and did not write down — which becomes indistinguishable from a bug.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT id AS job, schedule, COALESCE(paused_reason, '— no reason given —') AS why FROM pulse_jobs WHERE removed_at IS NULL AND paused = 1 ORDER BY id
targets.queryText: SELECT id AS job, schedule, COALESCE(paused_reason, '— no reason given —') AS why FROM pulse_jobs WHERE removed_at IS NULL AND paused = 1 ORDER BY id

panels.title: Runtime against the declared budget
panels.description: `max_runtime_s` is the SIGKILL line (exit -9). A job whose worst run is already past half its budget is one slow night from being killed mid-work, which reads downstream as a failure with no output.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT j.id AS job, j.max_runtime_s AS budget_s, ROUND(MAX(r.duration_ms) / 1000.0, 1) AS worst_s, COUNT(CASE WHEN r.exit_code = -9 THEN 1 END) AS killed FROM pulse_jobs j JOIN pulse_runs r ON r.job_id = j.id WHERE j.removed_at IS NULL AND r.duration_ms IS NOT NULL GROUP BY j.id HAVING worst_s > j.max_runtime_s * 0.5 ORDER BY worst_s / j.max_runtime_s DESC LIMIT 15
targets.queryText: SELECT j.id AS job, j.max_runtime_s AS budget_s, ROUND(MAX(r.duration_ms) / 1000.0, 1) AS worst_s, COUNT(CASE WHEN r.exit_code = -9 THEN 1 END) AS killed FROM pulse_jobs j JOIN pulse_runs r ON r.job_id = j.id WHERE j.removed_at IS NULL AND r.duration_ms IS NOT NULL GROUP BY j.id HAVING worst_s > j.max_runtime_s * 0.5 ORDER BY worst_s / j.max_runtime_s DESC LIMIT 15

panels.title: Runs that can be traced to what they did
panels.description: `pulse_runs.actor_action_id` was declared in 2026-05-08 and NULL on all 56 051 rows until 2026-08-29 — the daemon never sent one, so a nightly job could not be joined to the session it started or the rows it wrote. It now carries the run's own uuid, which the child already receives as PULSE_RUN_ID and an AgentKit run adopts as its session uuid. `events` and `session` count what that key reaches. A run with 0 in both is honest: most jobs are plain subprocesses that emit nothing.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT r.job_id AS job, r.fired_at AS fired, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events e WHERE e.actor_action_id = r.actor_action_id) AS events, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agent_sessions s WHERE s.uuid = r.actor_action_id) AS session FROM pulse_runs r WHERE r.actor_action_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY r.fired_at DESC LIMIT 20
targets.queryText: SELECT r.job_id AS job, r.fired_at AS fired, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events e WHERE e.actor_action_id = r.actor_action_id) AS events, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agent_sessions s WHERE s.uuid = r.actor_action_id) AS session FROM pulse_runs r WHERE r.actor_action_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY r.fired_at DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Where the 56 000 rows are
panels.description: Not a health question — a cost one. `pulse_runs` is the second-largest table in wing.db, and one per-minute job owns most of it. Read this beside `tools/wing-status.py --cost` before proposing a retention rule.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT job_id AS job, COUNT(*) AS rows_held, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pulse_runs), 1) AS pct_of_table, MIN(fired_at) AS oldest FROM pulse_runs GROUP BY job_id ORDER BY rows_held DESC LIMIT 12
targets.queryText: SELECT job_id AS job, COUNT(*) AS rows_held, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pulse_runs), 1) AS pct_of_table, MIN(fired_at) AS oldest FROM pulse_runs GROUP BY job_id ORDER BY rows_held DESC LIMIT 12
